issue.title: keep-moving-marks KT1–KT8 1500-resident count 1000 ms wall-clock bound flakes under full npm test load

task_type_fields.evidence: Observed during the bob-cli-nh.7.1 intention-card landing on bob-plugins b1a655a plus uncommitted intention-card changes (none touch keep-moving marks). Full `npm test` (default parallel node --test, ~2150% CPU) failed this node once in two full runs: assertion `elapsed < 1000` at scripts/test-ledger-tools-keep-moving-marks.cjs:300 reported "1500 resident count took 1528.8 ms" (test duration 1857 ms). The first full run passed it. Running the file alone passed 6/6 tests three times in a row. Root cause looks like a single performance.now wall-clock sample with a 1000 ms bound that parallel suite load exceeds; the functional count assertion (large.count === residents.length) passed. Fail rate: 1 of 2 full parallel runs, 0 of 3 serial file runs. Stabilize the timing check without weakening the bounded-counting contract or blindly raising the budget (compare bob-cli-ki, bob-cli-io, bob-cli-km).

issue.creation_reason: The intention-card landing's full bob-plugins npm test failed this unrelated timing node once; it passes serially and no bead tracks this node.
